title: telemetry-ops-field-binder-weekly-2027-02-21
content:
Telemetry Ops — Field Binder notes (week of 2027-02-15 -> 2027-02-21)

Context: lightweight-weekly capturing standups, experiment logs, dashboard changes, and cost telemetry reconciliations. This is a working doc (iteration) — action items at the bottom.

Quick summary:
- Sampling experiment (dynamic prefix-based sampling) showed 12% cost drop on inference traces for hosted API routes while preserving 95th pct error attribution for top 5 customer flows.
- Dashboard widget refactor merged to staging; load time improved from 4.8s -> 2.1s for per-route heatmaps.
- Span-budget reconciliation uncovered an edge case where prefix-kv cache spans were double-counted across retry paths (OBS-421).
- Decision: temporarily raise sampling floor for telemetry-heavy routes and add a canary alert for trace-completeness regressions.

Meetings this week:
1) Telemetry Ops sync (Mon 2027-02-15, 10:00-10:45) — Maya, Ethan, Samir, Lena, Priya
   Agenda: sampling rollout, dashboard perf, span budget reconciliation
   Notes:
   - Samir: sampling A/B comparing fixed 1% vs dynamic prefix-sensitivity. Dynamic performed better on real-traffic microbench (reduced traces by 18% for model-serving endpoints).
   - Lena: identified double-count on spans when retry metadata lacked unique attempt-id; created OBS-421 to fix instrumentation.
   - Priya: cost dashboards show unexpected spike on Feb 12-13; traced to a scheduled canary job misconfigured to use full-trace capture. Fix deployed.
   - Action: add attempt-id to retry header emit (Samir, due 2027-02-25).

2) Dashboard WG (Wed 2027-02-17, 14:00-15:00) — Attendees: Maya, Lena, Jason (FE), Noor (product), Ethan
   - Jason presented refactor plan: break per-route heatmap into sharded queries + client-side stitching.
   - Load test (staging): 50 concurrent users -> median load 2.1s, 95th 3.7s. Previous median 4.8s.
   - Product requested a compact view for SRE with top-10 noisy spans. Noor to prototype widget.
   - Action: Jason to roll refactor to prod behind feature flag on 2027-02-24, gradual ramp.

3) Cost telemetry retro (Fri 2027-02-19, 11:00-12:00) — Maya, Finance (Rafael), Ethan, Priya
   - Rafael: wanted clearer mapping from token-cost -> trace counts for committed capacity customers.
   - We agreed on a new export mapping table (CSV) combining per-route token totals, average model qps, and trace-sample-rate.
   - Action: Maya + Rafael to draft mapping doc and export spec (due 2027-02-26).

Standup log snippets (daily, short):
- Mon 2027-02-15
  - Maya: finish rollout plan for sampling; coordinate with infra for feature flag gates.
  - Ethan: instrument attempt-id on retry paths; writing unit tests.
  - Samir: run sampling measurement job against last 7 days; produce comparison table.

- Tue 2027-02-16
  - Lena: prototype compact SRE widget; hit a CORS issue when pulling heatmap shards.
  - Jason: tuned DB queries for sharded heatmaps.
  - Priya: reverted canary job and started retro with infra.

- Wed 2027-02-17
  - Maya: ran baseline full-trace capture numbers for top-20 routes.
  - Ethan: opened PR to add attempt-id header and de-dup logic (PR #214).
  - Samir: verified sampling A/B logs; initial cost delta: -12% token billing on test cluster.

- Thu 2027-02-18
  - Jason: landed staging changes for dashboard refactor. Observed 60% fewer DB rows fetched per render.
  - Lena: UX iteration for compact widget — needs clearer span grouping.
  - Priya: validated that Dedicated customers unaffected by canary misconfig; still need export mapping.

- Fri 2027-02-19
  - Team: quick sync; prepared notes for Finance meeting.
  - Decision: delay global sampling flag change until attempt-id de-dup is live.

Experiment logs (sampling):
- Experiment name: dynamic-prefix-sampling-v3
- Hypothesis: infer-span sampling that weights on prefix entropy and latency variance will reduce stored traces while keeping signal for heavy flows.
- Method: side-by-side capture for 10% of traffic; trace-sampler outputs kept separate; compare top-k flow coverage and error attribution.
- Result summary: 12% reduction in stored trace volume; top-5 flows retained >98% of their error annotations; 2 routes showed reduced anomaly recall (follow-ups scheduled).
- Next step: add a small oversampling rule for routes with tail-error signals (Samir, 2027-02-28).

Span budget & instrumentation notes:
- Root cause of double-count: retry attempts emitted spans with identical span-id when attempt-id not present; aggregator dedup was disabled for historic reasons.
- Hotfix applied in staging: aggregator now checks attempt-id if present. Long-term fix: ensure attempt-id always present (Ethan).
- OBS-421 details: code pointers, affected services, test coverage requirement.

Dashboards and metrics:
- New widgets merged to staging: per-route compact list, top noisy spans (prod-flagged), token-cost crosswalk table.
- Performance: per-route heatmap latency improved 2.3x median.
- Short-term UX request: add a toggle to switch between sample-rate-normalized and raw-count views (requested by SRE).

Runbook & Alerts:
- Added canary alert: trace-completeness-drop (fires when sampled trace ratio for a route drops >30% relative to baseline over 5m).
- Added docs to runbook outlining triage steps: check sampler config -> validate attempt-id presence -> fallback to high-fidelity capture for 10m.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ethan Patel — add attempt-id header for retry instrumentation + unit tests (due 2027-02-25)
- Samir Gupta — implement oversampling rule for routes with tail-error signals and run follow-up A/B (due 2027-02-28)
- Jason Kim — roll dashboard refactor to prod behind feature flag; monitor DB row fetch counts and load (start 2027-02-24)
- Maya Chen + Rafael (finance) — draft export mapping (CSV spec) for token-cost -> trace counts (due 2027-02-26)
- Lena Ortiz — prototype compact SRE widget with grouping heuristics (due 2027-03-03)

Blockers:
- Some legacy services do not emit retry attempt-id (requires small SDK bump; coordination with platform-engineering).
- Query cost: despite sharding, some heavy routes still cause expensive joins for historical heatmaps; may need an OLAP pre-aggregate.

Notes for follow-up:
- Validate that Dedicated/private deployments obey sampling policy parity and document differences in the export mapping.
- Consider a small backward-compat shim in aggregator to avoid historical double-count until SDK rollout completes.
- Keep an eye on cost telemetry during Jason's prod rollout — set an automatic rollback threshold if DB rows or query time exceed 2x baseline.

Misc (quick links and refs):
- OBS-421 (instrumentation dedup): https://linear.app/redwood/issue/OBS-421-kv-cache-span-budget
- Sampling experiment logs (internal): link to dataset and Jupyter notebook in the PR (see PR #214)
- Staging dashboard runbook: confluence page linked above

End of week note — Maya: overall good progress; focus next week is getting attempt-id live and ramping dashboard refactor safely.
